Subject: Post-demo: privacy checklist, residency & DPA next steps

Hi Samira / Carlos — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and the asks we captured on our side so we can align with legal and infra: 

- High-level ask: MedWise will be the data controller for PHI/PII. You need a Privacy Addendum (DPA) with explicit controller/processor mapping.
- PII types discussed: patient name, MRN, DOB, limited clinical notes, provider identifiers. No full imaging files will be sent in pilot.
- Residency: primary requirement is US-only residency for processing and logs.
- Retention: you mentioned 10-year retention for records due to your healthcare policy; please confirm which data class must follow 10 years.
- Logging/audit: you asked for admin-scoped audit logs with token-level request traces; preference to limit who can view redacted outputs.
- Subprocessors: you asked for guaranteed notification if a subprocessor change or incident occurs — your initial ask was 24 hours.
- Breach notice: you requested a confirmed-notice window and playbook (we discussed 24–48 hours).

Attachments: I am attaching a draft DPA and a simplified data flow diagram so your legal & security teams can annotate: Redwood_DPA_v2_draft.pdf, data_flow_diagram.png (see attachments).

Next steps I propose:
1) Your confirmation on controller role and the specific retention class for the 10-year requirement.
2) We route the DPA draft to your legal; please send any redlines (I noted your legal alias above).
3) Schedule a 30–45 minute call with infra/security to go over KMS, residency, and logging controls — Dev, Laura, can you join?

Thanks — I will hold a tentative legal+infra slot on Thursday morning PT and will update once I hear back.

Best,

Avery Johnson

Thanks Avery — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from MedWise: 

- Confirmed: MedWise is the controller for all patient data transmitted to Redwood during pilot and later production.
- Retention: Regulated clinical records must be retained for 10 years (this applies to the patient record objects you labelled as "clinical notes"). Metadata (non-PII) can follow shorter retention.
- Residency: US-only processing is required for pilot and prod. That must include both model inference and associated logs.
- Encryption / KMS: We require customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest in production. Please confirm if Redwood supports a bring-your-own-KMS model in Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Audit logs: We need role-based access to logs and the ability to redact outputs for non-admins.
- Subprocessor notification: legal prefers a 24-hour notification window for any security-impacting subprocessor changes or incidents. We understand that operationally this may be tight; please indicate feasibility.
- Breach notice: MedWise legal requests initial acknowledgement within 24 hours and an incident notification with details within 72 hours for confirmed breaches.

I've attached a single doc with our initial DPA comments: MedWise_DPA_comments.pdf. Let's get the legal + infra call on the calendar — our CISO prefers Thurs 10:00–11:00 ET.

Samira Khan
Head of Security & Compliance | MedWise Health
samira.k@medwise.com | +1 (212) 555-0147

Subject: Re: Post-demo: privacy checklist, residency & DPA next steps

Looping in some quick technical feasibility notes from infra/engineering:

- Residency: US-only processing + logs is supported on Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments. Hosted API can be restricted to a US region, but we recommend Dedicated/Private for contractual residency guarantees and SOC/audit controls.
- KMS / encryption: We support customer-managed KMS in Private deployments (HSM/KMS integrations). For Dedicated we provide a managed KMS with an option for customer-provided keys in controlled engagements — would need this scoped in the DPA/addendum.
- Logs and redaction: Audit logging is configurable. We can preserve token-level traces for 90 days by default; retention can be extended up to 365 days with an enterprise config. Role-based access controls exist for who can view raw outputs; we can implement output redaction filters for non-admin roles.
- Subprocessor notice: operationally, a 24-hour guaranteed notification for all subprocessor changes is very aggressive. Typical industry practice is 30 days for general notifications and 24–48 hours for incident-specific notices where a security-impacting event has occurred. For breach incidents we can commit to an initial acknowledgment within 24 hours and a detailed update within 72 hours for confirmed incidents. 

Action items for Redwood infra:
- I will prepare a short tech addendum describing KMS options, log retention SLAs, and our subprocessor notice playbook (will attach to the DPA).
- Laura, can you confirm SOC2 evidence and current list of subprocessors for the DPA exhibit?

— Dev

Thanks — helpful notes all around. Short reply with proposed next steps so we have a concrete path forward: 

1) DPA redlines: Samira/legal, we'll accept your PDF comments. I'll circulate an updated DPA that includes a short tech addendum for KMS, log retention options, and a subprocessor notification clause. Expect the update by EOD Monday PT. (Attachment: Redwood_DPA_v2_draft.pdf will be updated.)
2) Subprocessor notice: Redwood proposes the following compromise for contract language: 24-hour initial incident acknowledgment for security-impacting events + 30-day prior notice for non-incident subprocessor changes. We'll capture both in the addendum.
3) KMS & Residency: Confirmed — Customer-managed KMS supported on Private, scoped option for Dedicated. We'll call this out and include integration requirements in the tech addendum.
4) Audit logs & retention: We'll propose default retention of 90 days with an enterprise-configurable up to 365 days; we will include a clause that admin roles are required to manage access and that customer can request output redaction controls.
5) Legal + infra call: Proposed slot Thu 13 May 2027, 10:00–10:45 PT (Samira had Thurs 10–11 ET which maps to this). I'll send a calendar invite once Samira confirms.
